description:
FILED s426 (Opus, found by the #388 consumer-3 probes).  PRE-EXISTING and
identical in the CODE path and the INTERPOLATION path â the two agree with
each other, they both diverge from perl.

REPRO (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):

    our @x = (1,2,3);
    our $r  = \@x;        # array ref
    our $rr = \$r;        # scalar ref TO an array ref
    my $u = eval { my $q = ${$r};   "[$q]" }; print $@ ? "DIED\n" : "$u\n";
    my $v = eval { my $q = $$rr[1]; "[$q]" }; print $@ ? "DIED\n" : "$v\n";
    my $w = eval { my $q = "$$rr[1]"; "[$q]" }; print $@ ? "DIED\n" : "$w\n";

    perl: DIED / DIED / DIED
    PCL:  [3]  / []   / []

`${$r}` on an ARRAY ref: p-cast-$ hands the referent back instead of
raising, so the array is read in scalar context (3 = its length).
`$$rr[1]` where the referent is a SCALAR ref: p-aref-deref indexes it and
answers undef.  p-cast-@ / p-cast-% DO have the referent check
(%p-scalar-referent-p, #163) and die correctly â p-cast-$ and the
p-*-deref element accessors do not.  Same family as the s426 slice fix
(task #420), which added the p-cast-@/p-cast-% container deref: the
CONTAINER is now checked, the ELEMENT accessors still are not.

SIDE EFFECT worth knowing: because `${$aref}` does not die, `"$$r->[1]"`
and `"${$r}->[1]"` now (s426) print the element where perl dies.  That is
this leniency, not the interpolation port â the port made the string agree
with the code, which is the port's whole point.

FIX SHAPE: give p-cast-$ and the p-aref-deref / p-gethash-deref family the
%p-scalar-referent-p / %p-wrong-referent-p checks p-cast-@ already carries
(rule 12: the missing case must not answer a value the program consumes).
COST TO MEASURE FIRST: this turns silent-undef into a die in whatever
code currently leans on it â run the gate-SET scan over both populations
before shipping, exactly as s372 requires for a widened checker.

ACCEPTANCE: the three rows above vs perl, plus the inverse guards
`my $s = \"S"; ${$s}` (must stay "S") and `my $a = [1,2]; $$a[1]`
(must stay 2).
title: PCL is LENIENT where perl is FATAL on a wrong-kind deref: "${$aref}" returns the array (perl dies "Not a SCALAR reference"), "$$scalarref_to_aref[1]" returns undef (perl dies "Not an ARRAY reference")
